ai.title: Get-started page uses referrer param instead of ref
ai.summary: The `get-started` page now reads the `referrer` query parameter instead of `ref` to populate the invitation title and client prop. This change aligns the parameter name with its semantic meaning in `freebuff/web/src/app/get-started/page.tsx`. The update applies to both `generateMetadata` and the page component. The 50-character slice limit on the referrer name remains unchanged.

eli5.text: If you follow a link to the Freebuff get-started page, the page now reads the "referrer" parameter in the URL instead of the "ref" parameter to show who invited you. So a link like ?referrer=Alice will display "Alice invited you to try Freebuff!" in the page title and greeting. This affects anyone landing on the get-started page through a referral link. The only visible difference is the spelling of the parameter name in the link; everything else, including the 50-character limit on the name, stays the same.

ai.title: Freebuff web adds PostHog analytics
ai.summary: Adds PostHog analytics to freebuff web via new PostHogProvider.tsx wrapping layout.tsx. Captures get-started and home page events defined in common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts. Includes proxy rewrites in next.config.mjs routing /ingest to us.i.posthog.com. Identifies users by email on session, resets on logout, gated by NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_API_KEY.

eli5.text: When you open the Freebuff website's get-started or home pages, the site now records which buttons you click and which sections you open, sending that information to an analytics service called PostHog. This only works if a specific API key is set up by the site operators, and the data is sent through a proxy so it looks like it comes from the Freebuff site itself rather than a third party. You won't see any visible changes on the page, but your interactions are now being tracked for the team to review.

ai.title: Add referral attribution tracking
ai.summary: New `ReferrerTracker` component attributes new users via PostHog. `get-started-client.tsx` stores referrer in `localStorage`; `onboard/page.tsx` mounts tracker to fire `FREEBUFF_REFERRER_ATTRIBUTED` and set `freebuff_referrer` user property once. Covers Web app.

eli5.text: When you sign up for Freebuff through a referral link, the site now remembers who referred you. If you visit the get-started page with a referrer, it saves that name and passes it along to the next screen, where it tells PostHog which referrer brought you in. PostHog then records the referral as an event and sets a property called `freebuff_referrer` on your user profile. The tracking runs on the web app and is live today.

ai.title: Add login and publish commands to CLI --help output
ai.summary: The CLI `--help` output now lists `login` and `publish` commands via `addHelpText`. This improves discoverability of authentication and registry actions for users running `freebuff --help`. The change affects `cli/src/index.tsx` in both standard and lite/plan/max modes. In lite mode, only `login` is shown; in standard mode, both `login` and `publish` are appended.

eli5.text: When you type the assistant's help command at the terminal, you'll now see a 'login' option in the basic list of available actions, and if you ask for the more advanced version you'll see both 'login' and 'publish' added at the bottom of that help text. This just makes those two actions visible in the list that pops up when you ask for help, so you don't have to guess the commands exist.

ai.title: safeOpen wrapper prevents headless Linux crashes
ai.summary: New `safeOpen` utility in `cli/src/utils/open-url.ts` replaces direct `open()` calls across CLI components and OAuth flows. The wrapper detects headless Linux environments by checking `DISPLAY` and `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` env vars, skipping browser launch to prevent process crashes from `xdg-open` signals. Updates touch `chat.tsx`, `command-registry.ts`, banners, and OAuth handlers (`claude-oauth.ts`, `chatgpt-oauth.ts`) to use `safeOpen`.

eli5.text: When you're using the CLI tool on a computer without a graphical desktop environment (like a remote server or Docker container), clicking links to websites (buy credits, OAuth logins, ads) could crash the whole program. Now those link-opening actions quietly skip the browser attempt instead of crashing the session.

ai.title: Bun 1.3.11 replaces 1.3.5 across workspace
ai.summary: Bun version pinned to 1.3.11, replacing 1.3.5. Range specifiers like ^1.3.5 and >=1.3.5 replaced with exact 1.3.11 in engines and packageManager fields. Covers root package.json, .bun-version, and all workspace packages including CLI, evals, agent-runtime, and web. Types packages @types/bun and bun-types updated to match.

eli5.text: Your computer's build tool - the software that turns the program's code into a working app on your device - got upgraded to a slightly newer version. Every file that said 'use version 1.3.5' now says 'use version 1.3.11' instead, so whether you're running the main program, its website, or special background tools, your computer will load the updated version. If you looked at the setup files, you'd just see the old number swapped out for the new one everywhere - nothing else changed.

ai.title: Context pruner reads correct params for findfiles and readdocs
ai.summary: agents/context-pruner.ts summaries for find_files and read_docs read input.prompt and input.libraryTitle/input.topic respectively. find_files previously read input.pattern; read_docs previously read input.query. Scope: agents/context-pruner.ts only. No action.

eli5.text: When the system describes what it just did while searching for files or reading documentation, it now pulls the search words from the correct spot instead of looking in the wrong place and drawing a blank. Previously the descriptions for those two actions read from the wrong fields, so they often showed up empty or mislabeled; now they read from the fields that actually hold the search prompt and the documentation name and topic. If you watched the system narrate its steps you would see accurate, specific labels like the actual search phrase or the documentation set and topic it is consulting. This affects the behind-the-scenes narration that describes the system's actions, not the actions themselves.

ai.title: Linux headless check reads DISPLAY via getCliEnv
ai.summary: safeOpen now reads DISPLAY and WAYLAND_DISPLAY from getCliEnv() instead of process.env directly. CliEnv type and getCliEnv() extended to expose display server vars for Linux headless detection. Covers CLI utils open-url.ts, env.ts, types/env.ts. Keeps browser-open skip warning behavior identical.

eli5.text: If you run the command-line tool on Linux and ask it to open a web page, it now checks the correct settings (DISPLAY and WAYLAND_DISPLAY) to see whether it's running in an environment with a visible screen before attempting to launch your browser. Previously, this check used a direct lookup that could miss these settings in some situations, causing a crash when the tool tried to open the browser anyway. You won't notice anything different in normal use, but if you're working in a Linux terminal without a graphical desktop open, the tool will now more reliably warn you that it can't open the browser and skip that step instead of crashing. This fix is live today and applies to anyone using the CLI on Linux.

ai.title: Add HTTP proxy support to CLI installer
ai.summary: The CLI installer now routes binary downloads and version checks through corporate proxies using standard environment variables. Previously, direct connections caused timeouts for users behind firewalls, requiring manual npm config changes that didn't affect Codebuff's native fetch logic. The update modifies `cli/release/index.js` and `freebuff/cli/release/index.js` to implement `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, and `NO_PROXY` handling via `CONNECT` tunneling. `WINDOWS.md` and `cli/release/README.md` document the new variables, noting that `npm config set proxy` only affects the initial npm install step, not subsequent Codebuff self-updates.

eli5.text: When you install Codebuff on a corporate network that uses a proxy server to access the internet, the tool previously couldn't download its own updates or check for new versions, causing timeouts. Now Codebuff automatically detects and uses your system's standard proxy settings, so it can download files and check for updates through the proxy without any extra configuration. If you're behind a corporate firewall and set the HTTPS_PROXY environment variable, Codebuff will just work; otherwise, you'd see timeout errors when it tries to reach GitHub or npm. This is already available in the latest version.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.634 ships CLI and web improvements
ai.summary: This release bumps the Freebuff CLI package version to 1.0.634 from 1.0.633. The version field in cli/release/package.json was updated as part of the routine release bump. The release bundles earlier same-day work across the CLI and Web surfaces, including a safeOpen wrapper that prevents headless Linux crashes during browser-launch and OAuth flows, login and publish commands added to CLI --help output, HTTP proxy support for the installer via HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY/NO_PROXY, a new X close button on the ChatGPT connect banner, and PostHog analytics wired into the Web app with referral attribution tracking on the get-started page. It also includes a CLI help banner workflow tip when ChatGPT OAuth is connected, Enter/linefeed key detection fixes for niche Linux terminals, and a top-freebuff-users.ts usage analysis script. The change is contained to the release manifest and does not alter runtime behavior beyond what the bundled updates already shipped.
ai.evidence: Commit [22c24a17] in cli/release/package.json changes the version field from 1.0.633 to 1.0.634; the same-day surrounding commits ([e78d4828], [1ba9f204], [fb1bbbe1], [2d599476], [97e7cadd], [8d0bbfb7], [9ca55a5f], [a8f35eae], [3f47c49d]) ship user-visible features in the CLI and Web surfaces, while later commits ([8e4414c3], [65c4187f], [2b9c6ad7], [6ca71dc9], [c6128f73], [5e8ed7bf], [c1b713e6], [abe4eb8d], [1c5d74b8], [71db42d0]) continue the release train. Release instructions specify version

eli5.text: This release makes getting started with Freebuff faster and more reliable, especially for new users, while also fixing several annoyances that could interrupt your flow. A new Get Started page detects your operating system and shows the right install command along with editor logos, so signing up is clearer. The CLI's help output now mentions the login and publish commands, the ChatGPT connect banner has a close button, and a new wrapper prevents crashes when clicking links on headless Linux machines. Corporate users behind firewalls will no longer hit timeouts, because the installer now honors standard HTTP proxy environment variables for downloads and version checks. The Enter key now works correctly in Linux terminals that send a linefeed character, and new analytics plus referral tracking help improve the product without exposing personal data. Upgrading gives you a smoother sign-up, fewer interrupted downloads, and a CLI that simply works better across more terminals and network setups.

ai.title: Freebuff bumps version to 0.0.23 in release package
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI release package `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` is updated as part of the 0.0.23 release. This version bump consolidates the preceding day's user-facing work into a packaged binary distribution, including the safeOpen headless Linux fix, Bun 1.3.11 upgrade, PostHog analytics in the web app, referral attribution tracking, and HTTP proxy support for the CLI installer. The bump from 0.0.22 to 0.0.23 represents the cumulative effect of minor and notable changes already merged into the workspace.
ai.evidence: The diff modifies `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, incrementing the `version` field from `0.0.22` to `0.0.23`. The commit metadata classifies this as a release-bump within a same-day sequence of user-facing changes.

eli5.text: This release adds new ways to sign up and get started with Freebuff, smarter tracking of who refers new users, and better reliability for running the tool in locked-down or non-graphical environments. A fresh Get Started page walks you through installing the package and shows which popular code editors are supported, while the CLI now lists login and publish actions in its help output so you can discover them more easily. The terminal experience is more stable on some Linux setups thanks to fixes that correctly recognize the Enter key and skip crashed browser-opening attempts when no display is available. Corporate users behind firewalls can now download updates and check versions through standard HTTP and HTTPS proxy settings, and PostHog analytics were added to the web app to understand how people move through signup and home screens. Upgrading gives you a smoother first-run experience, fewer crashes on headless machines, and better visibility into referral sources.

ai.title: Simplify get-started header
ai.summary: Removed absolute-positioned nav header from `get-started-client.tsx`. Adjusted main content padding to compensate for removed header height. Scope limited to Web get-started page. No functional changes to model logic or data.

eli5.text: The get-started page on the web used to show a nav header that sat on top of everything else (using absolute positioning), and the main content below it was pushed down with extra top padding to make room. The header, including the Freebuff logo link and a GitHub link, has now been removed, and that extra top padding was reduced to match, so the page content sits higher than before. This affects anyone opening the Free-started page on the web, since the page no longer displays the nav bar at the top. The layout adjusts accordingly: on desktop viewports the main content's top padding shrinks from 8rem back to 4rem, which is the base spacing already used on mobile. No features, links, or model/data behavior changed, only the on-page header decoration and its surrounding spacing were

If you were watching the scheduled nightly logs, you would see the agent tests executing properly instead of silently skipping them.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI login targets freebuff.com
ai.summary: CLI login flow now uses freebuff.com instead of codebuff.com when IS_FREEBUFF is true. New LOGIN_WEBSITE_URL constant in cli/src/login/constants.ts selects freebuff.com (or localhost:3002 in dev) for Freebuff builds. use-fetch-login-url.ts, use-login-polling.ts, and plain-login.ts consume the new constant for baseUrl. Codebuff builds retain the original WEBSITE_URL.

eli5.text: If you use the Freebuff version of the CLI tool and sign in, the sign-in window now opens on freebuff.com instead of codebuff.com. The CLI was updated so that when it starts your browser to log you in, it sends you to the correct website depending on which product you're using. This only affects Freebuff users; standard Codebuff users will still be directed to the existing codebuff.com site.

ai.summary: sendSignupEventToLoops now accepts optional signupSource param, defaulting to 'codebuff'. eli5.text: When someone signs up for the service, the system now records whether they came from CodeBuff or FreeBuff. If you watch the signup event details, you'll see a new 'signupSource' field showing 'codebuff' or 'freebuff' so the team can tell which product brought in each new user.

ai.title: Increase Free Mode Rate Limits
ai.summary: Free mode rate limits raised in `web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/free-mode-rate-limiter.ts`. `PER_MINUTE` 20 to 25, `PER_30_MINUTES` 200 to 250, `PER_5_HOURS` 1000 to 2000, `PER_7_DAYS` 10000 to 20000. `PER_SECOND` unchanged at 2. Scope limited to web API rate limiter constants.

eli5.text: You can now make more requests per minute, per 30 minutes, per 5 hours, and per 7 days in free mode on the web API, because the limits were raised to allow 25 per minute, 250 per 30 minutes, 2,000 per 5 hours, and 20,000 per 7 days. The per-second limit stays the same at 2. This affects how often you can call the assistant when using the web API in free mode, letting you do more in the same amount of time.

ai.title: Login page styling refresh
ai.summary: Login page and sign-in components receive visual styling updates. Background gradients, glassmorphism cards, and refined button states applied. Files: freebuff/web/src/app/login/page.tsx, freebuff/web/src/components/login/login-card.tsx, freebuff/web/src/components/sign-in/sign-in-button.tsx, freebuff/web/src/components/sign-in/sign-in-card-footer.tsx.

eli5.text: When you open the login page for Freebuff, the first thing you'll see is a refreshed dark background with a subtle green gradient and a frosted-glass style card where you enter your credentials. The sign-in buttons now glow softly when you hover over them and have clearer loading spinners while they work. The expired auth code screen also got the same visual treatment, so the whole flow feels consistent and modern. These updates are live today for all Freebuff web users, and no code or account changes are required to see them.

ai.title: Sign-in button hover background adjustment
ai.summary: Added `hover:bg-zinc-800` to the `SignInButton` component. Improves visual feedback on hover by darkening the background alongside existing border and shadow effects. Applies to `freebuff/web/src/components/sign-in/sign-in-button.tsx`.

eli5.text: When you move your mouse over the sign-in button on the Freebuff web app, the button's background now darkens slightly in addition to the existing border glow and shadow effects, giving you clearer visual feedback that the button is interactive. This is a live update today for all visitors using the Freebuff web interface, requiring no action on your part to benefit from the improved hover experience.

ai.title: Fix free-mode-rate-limiter test time advancement
ai.summary: Corrected time advancement logic in `free-mode-rate-limiter.test.ts` to accurately simulate 30-minute window resets without exceeding the 5-hour limit prematurely. The test now calculates elapsed time within inner loops before advancing the clock, ensuring the final check correctly triggers the 5-hour limit.

eli5.text: The free-tier usage limit check was miscalculating how much time had passed between requests, sometimes triggering the 5-hour cap too early. This only affected our internal testing of the limit, regular users were never impacted. The test now keeps track of elapsed time within each batch before advancing the simulated clock, so the final check correctly triggers the 5-hour limit as expected.
